# Koatty

> TypeScript framework with dependency injection, AOP and HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC and GraphQL support.

## Framework documentation

- [Overview](README.md): Framework introduction and documentation index.
- [Guides](guide/): Application structure, configuration and existing decorators.
- [Protocols](protocols/): Protocol-specific controller and server guidance.
- [Migration](migration/): Compatibility and migration notes.

- [Security Profile](guide/security.md): resolveProfileName (KOATTY_ENV || NODE_ENV), strict/standard/development, fail-closed defaults (DTO whitelist, WS origin, /metrics loopback trust, ops token, TLS 1.2, request IDs), legacyDefaults scope.
- [MCP Server](extensions/mcp.md): koatty_mcp exposes @Validated Service methods as MCP tools/resources/prompts; destructive tools require human approval (durable single-use tickets bound to the caller fingerprint); scope checks on every transport.
- [LLM Client](extensions/llm.md): koatty_llm routes logical model names across providers with failover, breaker, atomic token budgets, exact-match caching, structured output via koatty_validation DTOs, and an in-process tool loop.
- [AI Guard](extensions/guard.md): koatty_guard runs masking -> content inspection -> rate limit -> approval -> audit in a single @Around aspect; masking uses exact normalized key names; audit does not record prompt/output content by default.
- [v4 to v5 Migration](migration/v4-to-v5.md): experimental API removals (UseGuard/UseInterceptor/runSync), HTTP/3 moved to koatty_http3, DTO instance transformation, tightened security defaults, peer alignment to ^5.

## Application tooling

Use the project's installed koatty_cli 5.x binary (`koatty manifest`, `koatty mcp`).
A manifest is static: check collectionMode and unresolved before treating information as complete.
DTO/config schemas are JSON Schema; config.schemaSource distinguishes declared and inferred constraints.
MCP writes require a plan issued in the same session and an explicit dryRun:false after client approval.
koatty_test executes project code and is not read-only or guaranteed idempotent.
Use existing Controller/Mapping, Autowired, Before/After/Around and Validated decorators.
Do not introduce Guard/Interceptor decorator aliases to describe existing middleware or aspects.
